Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words

- Orientation: landscape view of an opened bifolium (central fold visible as a vertical crease at about x=1060 of the overview). Parchment, heavily stained, browned, with losses along all edges, holes near the fold and in the right leaf; repaired with tissue at left. A colour/grey scale at left.
- Two leaves, each with two columns of text: left leaf cols at ~x 450-700 and ~720-980; right leaf cols at ~x 1150-1430 and ~1440-1720. About 45-50 lines per column visible (top lines partly lost/stained).
- Script: small, heavily abbreviated cursive bookhand (looks like a later medieval cursive, anglicana-type forms with looped ascenders); single scribe apparently throughout. Brown ink, much faded.
- Right leaf, col. a, about two-thirds down: a large decorated initial (P? with cross-hatched bowl, drawn in ink, not obviously coloured) followed by a heading in larger, more formal script reading roughly "...rior / pars est" (tentative: "[P]rior pars est" or "[P]rima pars est"). This looks like a section opening.
- Small marks/paraphs in margin of right leaf (at ~x 1115, y 375 and y 625) -- possibly marginal signs or nota marks.
- Left leaf col. a: lines are shorter/indented on the left in the lower half (text appears to start further right), possibly due to damage or a left-justified layout lost to stain.
- No running titles visible (top margin damaged). No visible interlinear gloss; some superscript abbreviation letters.
- Tentative interpretation: continuous scholastic prose (possibly commentary/treatise); vocabulary on the overview suggests natural philosophy (words like "globus/glob(us)", "lumen", "motor/motus" seem visible) -- to be checked on tiles.
